subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this `gateway.peers` session-tool routing shape now, or wait for a broader federation contract before adding cross-gateway session sends/spawns?
rationale: The PR changes gateway trust boundaries, remote session ownership, message delivery, and config surface, and the right answer depends on maintainer security/product intent rather than a purely mechanical patch.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Define peer identity, allowed URL policy, token scopes, replay/idempotency, and session visibility before landing any core cross-gateway session routing.

options.title: Narrow and repair this PR
options.body: If maintainers accept `gateway.peers`, require the branch to preserve raw `gatewayUrl` allowlisting, fix the remote spawn protocol shape, define tokenless-peer behavior, and provide live proof.

options.title: Defer to federation FRD
options.body: Hold or close this implementation in favor of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 if narrow peer routing is not the desired core contract.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, allowed URL policy, token scopes, replay/idempotency, and session visibility before landing any core cross-gateway session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for session-tool ownership and gateway URL policy points to this owner candidate.
